attack_mechanism: Corrupting `openMSP430.execution_unit_0.alu_0.alu_add_inc` during target calculation changes one or more bits of the value presented to the software-PC input. This mechanism uses the chain `openMSP430.execution_unit_0.alu_0.alu_add_inc -> openMSP430.execution_unit_0.alu_0.alu_out_nxt -> openMSP430.execution_unit_0.register_file_0.reg_dest_val_in -> openMSP430.frontend_0.pc_nxt -> openMSP430.frontend_0.pc`. `openMSP430.execution_unit_0.alu_0.alu_add_inc` contributes data or a selector to this computed target; the relevant assignment conditions include `openMSP430.execution_unit_0.register_file_0.inst_bw`, `openMSP430.frontend_0.pc_sw_wr`. For computed control transfers, the ALU and register-file datapaths produce `reg_dest_val_in`, which becomes `pc_sw` when R0 is the destination or a CALL requests a PC write. At the following PC write, execution is redirected to an unintended aligned or misaligned address.

Injecting a transient or stuck fault into `openMSP430.frontend_0.inst_to_1hot` before `pc` is enabled can add the wrong increment or prevent the expected increment. This mechanism uses the chain `openMSP430.frontend_0.inst_to_1hot -> openMSP430.frontend_0.inst_alu -> openMSP430.execution_unit_0.alu_0.alu_out_nxt -> openMSP430.execution_unit_0.register_file_0.reg_dest_val_in -> openMSP430.frontend_0.pc_nxt -> openMSP430.frontend_0.pc`. `openMSP430.frontend_0.inst_to_1hot` affects `fetch`, instruction length, or the instruction-state decision used by this sequential increment; the relevant assignment conditions include `openMSP430.frontend_0.inst_alu`, `openMSP430.execution_unit_0.register_file_0.inst_bw`, `openMSP430.frontend_0.pc_sw_wr`. With no software PC write and no interrupt-vector state active, `pc_nxt` falls through to `pc_incr = pc + {14'h0, fetch, 1'b0}`. The next instruction is skipped, repeated, or fetched from an unintended address.

A transient bit flip or forced value on `openMSP430.frontend_0.inst_to_1hot` before the next `mclk` edge can substitute a false target or assert the software-write selection on the wrong instruction. This mechanism uses the chain `openMSP430.frontend_0.inst_to_1hot -> openMSP430.frontend_0.exec_no_wr -> openMSP430.execution_unit_0.reg_dest_wr -> openMSP430.frontend_0.pc_nxt -> openMSP430.frontend_0.pc`. `openMSP430.frontend_0.inst_to_1hot` participates in forming or qualifying that software-PC path; the relevant assignment conditions include `openMSP430.execution_unit_0.register_file_0.pc_sw_wr`. During a CALL, jump, or instruction that writes R0, `pc_sw_wr` has priority in the `pc_nxt` multiplexer and selects `pc_sw`. The corrupted target is captured in `pc`, redirecting control flow, skipping intended instructions, or executing an unintended basic block.
